components.name: alacritty_terminal
components.role: VT emulator: grid, colours, cursor, modes, alternate screen and scrollback for the integrated terminal
components.integration: Rust crate linked only by kinein-core. Only the Term/Grid/parser surface is used; the crate's own tty, event_loop and thread modules are unused because the PTY stays with portable-pty. Replaces the vt100 emulator and the handwritten DECSCUSR tracker built on vte.

version.reason: Current stable release; MSRV 1.85 matches the project. Same emulator that backs Alacritty and Zed, and it re-exports the vte 0.15 the core already resolved.

maintenance.statusAtReview: Official Alacritty project; emulator in production use for years

runtimeSecurity.notes: The crate ships a tty module capable of spawning processes, but Kinein never calls it; sessions are created by portable-pty and only raw bytes reach the emulator.

scopeControls: Only Term, Grid and the ANSI Processor are used; tty/event_loop/thread stay unused
VoidListener: the core polls the grid instead of consuming emulator events
Scrollback bounded by Config::scrolling_history (5000 lines)
No CLI name, prompt text or user content is interpreted
Grid, modes and cursor share one mutex snapshot per frame
event.terminal.render contract unchanged by the swap
verification: Contract preserved: cursor/modes/scrollback/spans identical in the typed event
DECSCUSR shapes and blink, including sequences split across PTY chunks
Wide-char cell width, combining marks and ANSI colour mapping unit tests
End-to-end stdio probe: scrollbackMax, absolute scroll echo, clamping and multi-session
Strict clippy, full workspace tests and the C++/QML gates

components.name: rustix
components.role: Safe `access(2)` for the `serial` domain: tells whether the user can read and write a serial device node WITHOUT opening it (opening asserts DTR/RTS on most USB-UART bridges and resets the board)
components.integration: Rust crate linked only by kinein-core, one call site in serial.rs (`rustix::fs::access`). Declared with default-features = false and features ["std", "fs"]. Chosen over a stat()-based check because access(2) honours POSIX ACLs, which is how udev's TAG+="uaccess" grants the seat user access without any group; a mode-bit heuristic would report `root:dialout 0660` as writable for a user outside dialout, or as denied for a user covered by the ACL.

version.reason: Already resolved at 1.1.4 in Cargo.lock as a transitive dependency of portable-pty (rustix-openpty) and alacritty_terminal (polling) before this adoption; declaring it directly adds no crate and no second version.

license.spdx: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
license.source: crates.io version metadata for 1.1.4, read on 2026-09-11; MIT and Apache-2.0 are already in deny.toml

maintenance.statusAtReview: Active: Bytecode Alliance project, latest release 2026-02-22; it is the syscall layer under std-adjacent crates such as tempfile and the async-io stack.

runtimeSecurity.notes: It is a thin wrapper over Linux syscalls (raw syscalls or libc, chosen by the crate's backend); the `unsafe` lives inside it and none in this repository (#![forbid(unsafe_code)] stays). Kinein calls only fs::access, which reads nothing and writes nothing.

cost.notes: Measured with `cargo tree -i rustix` on 2026-09-11: the crate was already in the graph via polling and rustix-openpty; the direct declaration only widens its feature set by `fs`.

components.verification: cargo deny check (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) green on the real workspace with the crate declared, 2026-09-11; the `serial` tests exercise access() against 0o000, 0o060 and 0o600 nodes
